newsitem.title: USA: Union Texas Q1 up on higher crude oil prices.
newsitem.headline: Union Texas Q1 up on higher crude oil prices.

text.p: Union Texas Petroleum Holdings Inc on Wednesday said it attributed higher first quarter earnings to increased sales prices for crude oil, liquefied natural gas and natural gas and higher crude oil sales volumes in the North Sea.
Earlier, the company reported first quarter 1997 earnings of $0.74 per share, up from $0.54 per share a year ago.

"In the first three months of 1997, we benefited from an eight percent rise in our worldwide oil prices over 1996's same period, averaging $19.45 per barrel in 1997's first quarter compared to $17.93 a year ago," said chairman and chief executive John Whitmire.

In the North Sea, gas sales volumes rose 33 percent in 1997's first three months over the same period a year ago as a result of exceptionally cold weather in the United Kingdom and continental Europe, the company said.

The firm sees liquified natural gas, or LNG, supplied by Union Texas and its co-venturers to an Indonesian LNG plant declining by near 15 percent in 1997 compared to 1996 due to the reduction of deliveries under the venture's first contract in which the venture had a higher participation interest.

Union Texas said it expects to participate in 25 to 30 exploration wells this year, up from 13 in 1996. It added that the majority of 1997 exploration wells will begin drilling in the second half of the year.
